statement: Appendix research gathered 2026-08-29 via WebFetch of primary sources only; web-search budget (200) exhausted partway through Part A and curl egress blocked, so coverage biases toward man7/kernel.org/Microsoft Learn/IETF/W3C and some items are missing rather than absent.
research_needed: Re-run searches for gaps listed in 'What I skipped' (L364-385) with search budget and unblocked egress.

statement: Appendix file is a raw subagent transcript output (agent id and token usage trailer appended), not an edited normative document; its design recommendations are labelled synthesis/inference by the author.

Dating anchors verified 2026-08-28/29: Linux mainline 7.2, stable 7.2.2, LTS 6.18/6.12/6.6/6.1/5.15/5.10; Go 1.26 current; Python docs 3.14.7; PNG Third Edition W3C Rec 2025-06-24; POSIX pax in IEEE 1003.1-2024.
research_needed: Decide which kernel/OS minimums Entrybound targets; anchors date all version-specific statements.
decision_needed: What minimum Linux kernel, macOS, and Windows versions does Entrybound support for extraction confinement features?

statement: cap-std 4.0.3 was released 2026-08-27 (the version Entrybound pins).
research_needed: Track cap-std release cadence and security advisories as a longevity/dependency risk.

statement: statx(2) exposes atime, btime, ctime, mtime each as signed 64-bit seconds plus 32-bit nanoseconds; STATX_BTIME is best-effort and only returned if the filesystem supplies it.
No Linux syscall sets birth time: utimensat(2) sets only atime/mtime and ctime is set implicitly by the kernel, so a Linux extractor can record btime but never restore it.
research_needed: Confirm no newer kernel API (e.g. via fs-specific ioctl) permits btime setting on Linux 7.x.

statement: Recommendation: format should mark btime as capture-only with an explicit per-platform 'not restorable' declaration rather than silently dropping it.
research_needed: Check Entrybound FidelityReport / metadata namespaces for btime capture-only and restorability declaration.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound capture btime, and how is non-restorability reported per target platform?

statement: statx stx_attributes carries flags COMPRESSED, IMMUTABLE, APPEND, NODUMP, ENCRYPTED, VERITY (5.5+), DAX (5.8+), MOUNT_ROOT (5.8+), WRITE_ATOMIC (6.11+), suggested as a natural source for archive-level file flags.
research_needed: Decide which statx attributes are semantically meaningful to archive vs. volume-local.
decision_needed: Which Linux file attribute flags (immutable/append/nodump etc.) does Entrybound capture and restore, and at what criticality?

statement: ext4 base 128-byte inode stores atime/ctime/mtime/dtime/crtime as 32-bit seconds; _extra fields exist only for inodes larger than 128 bytes, using low 2 bits to extend seconds to 34 bits and upper 30 bits for nanoseconds.
ext4 extra epoch bits map timestamps across 1901-2446 in 68-year bands; the maximum representable ext4 timestamp is in 2446.
A 128-byte-inode ext4 has no _extra fields: second granularity, ends 2038, and no i_crtime; 256-byte-inode ext4 gives nanoseconds and range to May 2446. Inode size must not be assumed.
Timestamp fidelity is a per-filesystem property that the archive should record rather than assume (e.g. source granularity and range of the capturing filesystem).
research_needed: Check whether Entrybound records source filesystem timestamp precision; measure detection feasibility of inode size / fs granularity from userspace in safe Rust.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound record capture-filesystem timestamp granularity, and how is it detected?

statement: V5 XFS without bigtime: inode timestamps 1901-12-13 to 2038-01-19, quota timers 1970 to 2106; with bigtime (kernel 5.10) a 64-bit ns counter covering 1901-12-13 to 2486-07-02.
Unverified whether current mkfs.xfs enables the bigtime feature by default.
research_needed: Check current xfsprogs mkfs.xfs defaults from primary source.

statement: btrfs timestamp encoding, range and precision were not researched.
research_needed: Read btrfs on-disk format docs for timestamp width/precision/range.

statement: Widely repeated claim that APFS stores create/mod/change/access time as uint64 nanoseconds since 1970 UTC is unverified; Apple File System Reference (j_inode_val_t p.73) exists but was not read; Apple FAQ omits granularity.
refines_or_supersedes: Challenges widely-repeated APFS timestamp claim (external folklore)
evidence_in_source: none; primary source located but unread
research_needed: Read Apple File System Reference PDF p.73 j_inode_val_t.

statement: NTFS FILETIME is a 64-bit count of 100-ns intervals since 1601-01-01 UTC with no documented range bound; FAT creation time resolution is 10 ms.
NTFS records last-access time at 1-hour resolution, so NTFS atime is low-fidelity despite the 100-ns field width.
research_needed: Decide whether atime is captured at all and how its source precision is tagged on Windows.
decision_needed: Is atime captured/restored by default, given NTFS 1-hour resolution and atime volatility?

statement: ReFS timestamp encoding and ReFS specifics were not researched.
research_needed: Research ReFS timestamp and metadata semantics from Microsoft primary docs.

statement: ustar stores mtime in a 12-byte octal field maxing at 8589934591 seconds (about 2242-03-16) and has no atime/ctime/btime fields.
research_needed: Legacy tar export profile must handle timestamps beyond ustar range (use pax or report LOSSY).

statement: POSIX pax extended header records use length/keyword=value format; standard keywords include atime, mtime, uid, gid, uname, gname, path, linkpath, size, charset, comment, hdrcharset; values are decimal strings with unbounded precision/range; typeflag x per-file, g global.
pax keywords of only lowercase letters, digits and periods are reserved for standardization; vendor extensions use VENDOR.keyword, so any Entrybound pax extension keywords must be uppercase-prefixed.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound tar export/sidecar keywords for compliance.
decision_needed: What vendor prefix will Entrybound use for pax extension keywords, if any?

statement: ctime is not in the retrieved POSIX pax standard keyword list; GNU tar emits it as an extension.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (pax spec), GNU behaviour stated
research_needed: Confirm GNU tar ctime keyword spelling and reader behaviour for import reconciliation.

statement: Recommendation: store timestamps as signed 64-bit seconds plus unsigned 32-bit nanoseconds; never model timestamps as a single float.
research_needed: Compare with Entrybound canonical timestamp encoding in the metadata namespace spec.

statement: Recommendation: tag each timestamp with a source-precision enum (second / 100 ns / microsecond / nanosecond).
research_needed: Check whether Entrybound has a precision tag; define the enum set including FAT 2-second/10ms and NTFS atime 1-hour cases.
decision_needed: Does the Entrybound timestamp record carry a source-precision tag, and which values?

statement: Recommendation: carry an explicit per-timestamp 'restorable' bit.
research_needed: Decide if restorability is archive data (capture-time) or extraction-time FidelityReport output.
decision_needed: Is restorability recorded in the archive or computed at extraction per target platform?

statement: Linux/POSIX uid_t/gid_t are 32-bit; POSIX pax carries both numeric ids (uid, gid) and names (uname, gname), with names taking precedence when resolvable.
Recommendation: copy the pax ownership model of recording both numbers and names with names preferred when resolvable.
decision_needed: On restore, do names or numeric ids take precedence in Entrybound ownership restoration?

statement: idmapped mounts introduce three ID spaces (userspace uid_t, filesystem kuid_t, mount-level vfsuid_t), attached per mount via mount_setattr().
Unverified which kernel version introduced idmapped mounts (commonly cited 5.12 not confirmed).
research_needed: Confirm from kernel release notes.

statement: A uid read through an idmapped mount is a view, not on-disk identity; inside a user namespace uid 0 is a host subuid, so the same archive restored in two namespaces yields different on-disk owners.
A high-fidelity format must record which ID space a numeric owner came from, or record names only and treat numbers as advisory.
research_needed: Determine whether ID space can be detected from userspace (statx STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT, mount info) in safe Rust.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound record the ID space of captured uid/gid, or treat numeric ids as advisory?

statement: Windows ownership is a variable-length SID; local-account SIDs are machine-specific and meaningless across machines; owner and primary-group SIDs live inside the security descriptor.
There is no lossless mapping between POSIX uid and Windows SID.
Recommendation: model ownership as a tagged union posix{uid,gid,uname,gname,id_space} or windows{owner_sid,group_sid,sddl_or_binary_sd}.
research_needed: Compare with Entrybound ownership metadata namespace design.
decision_needed: Is ownership a tagged union of platform-specific records in the Entrybound EAM?

statement: The spec should declare that cross-platform ownership restore is a policy decision, not a representable value.
decision_needed: What is Entrybound's default cross-platform ownership restore policy (ignore, map by name, refuse)?

statement: POSIX mode bits include setuid, setgid and sticky; Python's tar extraction filter deliberately clears those high bits and group/other write on extraction.
Recommendation: extractor default should match Python tar filter by clearing setuid/setgid/sticky and group/other write bits unless explicitly preserving.
research_needed: Check Entrybound dangerous-restoration policy defaults for setuid/setgid/sticky and group/other write.
decision_needed: Does default Entrybound extraction strip setuid/setgid/sticky and group/other write, and which flag restores them?

statement: POSIX ACLs are stored as system.posix_acl_access and system.posix_acl_default extended attributes.
POSIX ACL xattr encoding: 4-byte little-endian a_version (0x0002) header then 8-byte entries {le16 e_tag, le16 e_perm, le32 e_id}; ACL_UNDEFINED_ID is -1; little-endian on every architecture.
An archiver may copy the POSIX ACL xattr blob byte-portably, but any parser of it must decode little-endian explicitly and never use host byte order.
research_needed: If Entrybound parses ACLs into a structured record, add big-endian test vectors.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound store POSIX ACLs as opaque xattr blobs or as parsed canonical records?

statement: acl(5): entry types USER_OBJ, USER, GROUP_OBJ, GROUP, MASK, OTHER; when a MASK entry exists the st_mode group bits reflect the mask, and changing mode bits modifies ACL entries and vice versa.
Restore order is semantically load-bearing (chmod then set-ACL differs from set-ACL then chmod); the spec must normatively fix the order, standard answer being set ACL last.
research_needed: Test ordering effects on ext4/XFS/btrfs; check Entrybound restore pipeline ordering.
decision_needed: What normative metadata restore order does Entrybound fix (mode, ownership, ACL, xattrs, timestamps)?

statement: NFSv4 ACEs are type:flags:principal:permissions with types allow/deny/audit/alarm, inheritance flags, 13 file / 14 directory permissions, and special principals OWNER@, GROUP@, EVERYONE@.
NFSv4 ACLs differ structurally from POSIX ACLs (no mask, ordered evaluation, explicit deny); no faithful conversion exists, so the model must treat them as distinct types.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound v1 capture NFSv4 ACLs at all, and as a distinct namespace from POSIX ACLs?

statement: A Windows SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR holds owner SID, primary group SID, DACL, SACL and control bits; Microsoft says applications must not directly manipulate its contents.
SDDL text form (O: G: D: S:) round-trip caveat: conditional ACEs and resource attributes use a separately documented SDDL grammar.
Recommendation: for archival fidelity store the self-relative binary security descriptor (MS-DTYP wire form) and treat SDDL only as a human-readable annotation.
research_needed: Assess whether reading/writing binary SDs is feasible in safe Rust (windows-sys requires unsafe FFI); SACL capture needs SeSecurityPrivilege.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound capture Windows security descriptors, including SACL, and in binary or SDDL form?

statement: macOS ACL entries are identity:allow|deny:permission with enforced canonical order local deny, local allow, inherited deny, inherited allow, plus file/directory permission sets and inheritance flags.
Structural resemblance of macOS ACLs to NFSv4 ACLs (deny entries, ordering, inheritance, no mask) is the author's inference; chmod(1) documents no relationship.
research_needed: Determine whether macOS and NFSv4 ACLs can share one model type or need distinct namespaces.

statement: Linux user.* xattrs are governed by file permission bits and restricted to regular files and directories (not symlinks, devices, FIFOs).
research_needed: Validate that Entrybound rejects/reports user.* xattrs on symlinks or special files at capture and restore.

statement: trusted.* xattrs need CAP_SYS_ADMIN; system.* holds kernel objects such as ACLs with filesystem-specific policy; security.* holds LSM labels and capabilities with per-attribute policy.
decision_needed: Which Linux xattr namespaces does Entrybound capture and restore by default vs. only with privileged/explicit opt-in?

statement: Linux VFS xattr limits: name up to 255 bytes, value up to 64 KB, listxattr list up to 64 KB.

ext2/3/4 require all xattr names and values of a file to fit in a single filesystem block (1024-4096 bytes); btrfs caps name+value+overhead at nodesize (16 KB default); XFS and btrfs have no practical count limit.
A 64 KB xattr captured from XFS cannot be restored to ext4 at all.
The format needs a per-xattr size and a declared failure mode, and must surface the total-xattr budget as a constraint rather than discovering it at extraction time.
research_needed: Check Entrybound xattr record and declared metadata budgets; define behaviour when target fs rejects size (E2BIG/ENOSPC).
decision_needed: What is Entrybound's declared failure mode when an xattr cannot be restored due to target filesystem limits?

statement: A per-entry and per-archive xattr size budget (names up to 255 bytes, values up to 64 KB per VFS) should be declared as a resource bound.
decision_needed: What declared xattr name/value/total budgets does the Entrybound container enforce?

statement: security.capability has v1 (32-bit masks), v2 (Linux 2.6.25, 64-bit), v3 (Linux 4.14, adds namespace root uid); writing requires CAP_SETFCAP and the kernel picks v2 or v3 by writing namespace.
A v3 capability xattr encodes a rootid meaningful in only one user namespace, so it is not portable across namespaces even on one machine; must be treated as non-portable/dangerous.
research_needed: Check Entrybound criticality/danger classification for security.capability restoration.
decision_needed: Is security.capability restoration refused by default and gated behind an explicit privileged mode?

statement: SELinux label (security.selinux) internal format was not researched.
research_needed: Research SELinux context string format and restore semantics (relabel vs preserve).
decision_needed: Does Entrybound preserve, drop, or relabel security.selinux on restore?

statement: macOS setxattr documents ERANGE, E2BIG and ENAMETOOLONG (XATTR_MAXNAMELEN UTF-8 bytes) but no numeric size limits; max size is queried via pathconf _PC_XATTR_SIZE_BITS. XATTR_FINDERINFO_NAME must be exactly 32 bytes; XATTR_NOFOLLOW documented.
macOS numeric xattr size limits are undocumented (only pathconf _PC_XATTR_SIZE_BITS); XATTR_SHOWCOMPRESSION presence unverified.
research_needed: Measure pathconf _PC_XATTR_SIZE_BITS on APFS/HFS+ and read APFS reference XATTR_MAX_EMBEDDED_SIZE p.97.

statement: macOS named attributes of interest: com.apple.FinderInfo (32 bytes fixed), com.apple.ResourceFork, com.apple.quarantine, com.apple.provenance, com.apple.decmpfs.
Contents/format of com.apple.quarantine and com.apple.provenance could not be sourced from Apple primary documentation.
research_needed: Find Apple primary documentation or reverse-engineered reference for quarantine and provenance payloads.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound propagate macOS quarantine/provenance origin markers to extracted files?

statement: RFC 1740: AppleSingle magic 0x00051600, AppleDouble 0x00051607, version 0x00020000, 16-byte filler, 2-byte entry count, 12-byte {id,offset,length} descriptors; IDs 1 data fork, 2 resource fork, 3 real name, 4 comment, 9 Finder info.

The ._ filename convention is not defined in RFC 1740 (a MIME transmission format); it is documented behaviourally in ditto(1) as Carbon-compatible AppleDouble files on filesystems without native resource forks.
research_needed: Define how legacy import reconciles ._ members into native fork/xattr metadata.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound legacy import fold ._ AppleDouble members into the entry's forks/xattrs or keep them as plain files?

statement: NTFS alternate data stream full name is filename:streamname:streamtype; default stream is unnamed (filename::$DATA equals filename); stream names may use any filename-legal characters including spaces; $-prefixed stream types are NTFS-internal and cannot be created; enumerate with FindFirstStreamW/FindNextStreamW.
Microsoft documents no size or count limit for alternate data streams, so an archive must impose its own declared bounds on ADS count and size.
research_needed: Measure practical ADS count/size behaviour on NTFS and ReFS.
decision_needed: What declared ADS count/size budget does Entrybound enforce?

statement: Reparse data including tag and optional GUID cannot exceed 16 KB; a path may contain at most 63 reparse points; reparse points and extended attributes cannot coexist on one file; a directory reparse point requires an empty directory.
research_needed: Determine restore ordering implications: create reparse point before populating directory is impossible, so directory junctions must be created empty.

statement: Junctions (IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT) target directories only, store absolute paths and cannot cross volumes; symlinks (IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK) target files or directories, relative or absolute, can span volumes and need privilege to create since Vista; FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT opens the reparse point itself.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound restore Windows symlinks/junctions by default, and what happens without symlink-creation privilege?

statement: Because reparse points and NTFS extended attributes cannot coexist, an entry carrying both cannot be restored faithfully on NTFS; a declared conflict outcome is implied.
research_needed: Confirm with Windows test (WSL EAs plus reparse) and define reported loss.

statement: NTFS sparse files keep an internal list of zero regions; GetVolumeInformation tests support, GetCompressedFileSize gives allocated vs GetFileSize nominal size; disk quota is charged at nominal, not allocated, size.
FSCTL_SET_SPARSE / FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA / FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES details were not fetched, and ReFS sparse behaviour is not covered.
research_needed: Read FSCTL sub-pages; test sparse restore on NTFS and ReFS via safe Rust APIs.

statement: Zone.Identifier ADS uses a [ZoneTransfer] section with ZoneId 0 My Computer, 1 Local intranet, 2 Trusted sites, 3 Internet, 4 Restricted sites.
Mark of the Web applies only to files on NTFS, not FAT32.
Unverified which archive formats/tools propagate vs strip Mark of the Web to extracted members (7-Zip/ISO/VHD gaps are believed real but not primarily sourced).
research_needed: Test MOTW propagation by Windows Explorer ZIP, 7-Zip, tar.exe, ISO/VHD mount; source Microsoft docs.
decision_needed: Must Entrybound propagate the archive's MOTW to extracted members on Windows by default?

statement: An older IE doc covers only the HTML-comment form of MOTW ('saved from url=' within first 2048 bytes), not the ADS form.

NTFS supports per-directory case sensitivity (fsutil setCaseSensitiveInfo), introduced Windows 10 build 17107 (WSL inspection in 17692); the directory must be empty to change the flag; WSL 2 inherits the flag to new subdirectories, WSL 1 does not; applications may fail in case-sensitive directories.
research_needed: Decide whether extractor should ever enable per-directory case sensitivity to restore case-distinct names.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound refuse case-fold collisions on Windows, or optionally create case-sensitive directories (must be empty first)?

statement: Windows reserved names are CON PRN AUX NUL, COM1-COM9 plus superscript COM1-3 variants, LPT1-LPT9 plus superscript LPT1-3 variants; reservation applies even with extensions (NUL.txt, NUL.tar.gz).
research_needed: Verify Entrybound reserved-name check includes superscript digit variants and multi-extension forms.

statement: Windows forbids < > : " / \ | ? *, NUL and 0x01-0x1F in names (except within ADS names) and advises no trailing space or period.
MAX_PATH is 260 before Windows 10 1607; the \\?\ prefix disables all Win32 path parsing and normalization (. and .. become literal) and raises the limit to 32,767 characters.
macOS resource forks appear both as the com.apple.ResourceFork xattr and via the file/..namedfork/rsrc path; Finder info is com.apple.FinderInfo, exactly 32 bytes.
Apple has published no normative specification for the com.apple.decmpfs payload; all implementations are reverse-engineered; only ditto --hfsCompression/--nohfsCompression tooling is documented.
Recommendation: treat com.apple.decmpfs as opaque-blob-or-drop in the model; never attempt to synthesize it.
research_needed: Decide whether decmpfs files are captured as decompressed content (reading via normal file API) with the xattr dropped and loss reported.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound capture decmpfs as opaque xattr, drop it with a loss record, or ignore it?

statement: APFS firmlinks were not researched.
research_needed: Research firmlink representation and whether capture should treat them as directories or links.

statement: ditto(1) preserves resource forks and HFS metadata by default, and xattrs and ACLs by default since 10.5; --norsrc disables forks and implicitly xattrs, ACLs and quarantine; --rsrc and --extattr/--noextattr toggle independently.
ditto --sequesterRsrc stores resource forks and HFS metadata under __MACOSX in ZIP files so PKZip extraction finds them; __MACOSX/ entries are a deliberate documented convention.
research_needed: Define ZIP import reconciliation of __MACOSX/ AppleDouble members with their base entries.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound ZIP import reconcile __MACOSX/ sequestered metadata into native forks/xattrs, and does ZIP export emit it?

statement: Unverified: Apple bsdtar --disable-copyfile behaviour and exactly when macOS tar emits ._ members.
research_needed: Test macOS tar with and without COPYFILE_DISABLE / --disable-copyfile.

statement: libarchive ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_MAC_METADATA (restore via copyfile(3)) is ignored by default.
lseek SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA was added in Linux 3.1, supported by btrfs (3.1), OCFS (3.2), XFS (3.5), ext4 and tmpfs (3.8), NFS (3.18), FUSE (4.5), GFS2 (4.15).

Filesystems are not obliged to report holes accurately (written zeros may not be reported as holes) and every file has an implicit hole at its end; two archivers on different filesystems legitimately produce different sparse maps for byte-identical files.
Hole geometry is advisory, not content: sparse maps must not participate in content identity or determinism of logical file bytes.
evidence_in_source: synthesis from lseek(2) and libarchive SPARSE behaviour
research_needed: Check whether Entrybound identity roots (LAI/PCR) exclude sparse map; test identical-bytes-different-holes yields identical identity.
decision_needed: Is sparse layout excluded from Entrybound content identity and recorded only as advisory platform metadata?

statement: FIEMAP returns extent lists with flags LAST, UNWRITTEN (reads as zeros), DELALLOC (sets UNKNOWN), ENCODED, DATA_INLINE, UNKNOWN, SHARED; FIEMAP_FLAG_SYNC syncs first; physical offsets are unsafe to act on while mounted.
Recommendation: use SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA as the archiving primitive for hole detection; FIEMAP only for diagnostics.
research_needed: Check safe-Rust availability of SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA (rustix/cap-std) and Windows FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES equivalents.

statement: Old GNU sparse (tar 1.09, 1990): typeflag S, four inline {offset,size} entries, isextended flag chaining extension headers of 21 entries each, plus realsize.
GNU PAX sparse 0.0 (tar 1.14-1.15.1) repeats GNU.sparse.offset/numbytes keywords, violating POSIX last-occurrence semantics; non-GNU tars extract condensed form, i.e. silently wrong data.
research_needed: Legacy tar adapter must detect PAX 0.0 sparse and parse repeated keywords or refuse.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's tar import support GNU PAX 0.0 sparse, and how are repeated keywords handled vs POSIX last-wins?

statement: GNU PAX sparse 0.1 (tar 1.15.2) uses a single GNU.sparse.map offset,size list with real name in GNU.sparse.name, pointing the ustar name at a directory so foreign tars deposit the condensed file recoverably.
GNU PAX sparse 1.0 (tar 1.15.92) uses GNU.sparse.major/minor and moves the map into the data stream as newline-delimited decimals; it is the only GNU sparse variant that degrades safely.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (GNU tar manual) plus analysis
decision_needed: If Entrybound tar export emits sparse files, does it use PAX 1.0 only or densify?

location: A7 PyPI claim L150; Gaps L367
statement: The claim that PyPI banned sparse members in sdists in 2026 could not be verified: no 2026 PyPI blog post (seven enumerated) concerns sparse files or tar, and no Warehouse issue/PR was found.
refines_or_supersedes: Fails to verify (effectively refutes) the PyPI 2026 sparse-member ban premise posed to this research; any Entrybound document citing it should be corrected
evidence_in_source: negative search of primary source (blog.pypi.org enumeration)
research_needed: Search Warehouse repo/PyPI changelog directly; remove or correct any Entrybound citation of a PyPI sparse ban.

statement: Go CVE-2026-32288 (reported 2026-03-23): archive/tar Reader could allocate unbounded memory on crafted old-GNU sparse maps with many regions; fix caps extension blocks and total sparse entries across all encodings, targeted for Go 1.27.
research_needed: Fuzz Entrybound tar import adapter with many-sparse-region inputs; confirm entry caps across all sparse encodings.

statement: PyPI Warehouse PR #18492 (2026) hardens wheel ZIP parsing: rejects invalid framing, duplicate filenames, local-header/central-directory mismatches, trailing data, and multiple EOCD records; RECORD-mismatch rejection begins 2026-02-01.
research_needed: Ensure Entrybound ZIP import refuses/diagnoses the same ambiguity classes and ZIP export never produces them.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound ZIP import treat duplicate names, LH/CD mismatch, trailing data and multiple EOCD as REFUSED or as reconciled conflicts?

statement: A sparse map is simultaneously an unbounded-allocation vector, a way for declared logical size to diverge from stored bytes (zip-bomb-by-hole), and non-canonical because hole geometry is filesystem-dependent.
If sparseness is supported, the normative spec must bound the sparse map length.
decision_needed: What is the normative maximum sparse-map length / extent count per entry in Entrybound?

statement: A sparse map must be monotonic and non-overlapping and sum consistently with the declared logical size.
research_needed: Add conformance vectors for overlapping, unordered and size-inconsistent sparse maps.

statement: Place the sparse map in the data stream (PAX 1.0 style) rather than an unbounded header chain.
decision_needed: Where does Entrybound encode sparse extents (manifest record vs data stream), and is logical size vs stored size bounded against hole bombs?

statement: Declared logical size inflation via holes (zip-bomb-by-hole) must be bounded by declared resource budgets at extraction.
research_needed: Test extraction budget accounting of hole bytes (logical vs allocated) on sparse-capable and non-sparse targets.
decision_needed: Do Entrybound's total-logical-bytes budgets count holes, and does non-sparse target restore densify within budget?

statement: Python tarfile data filter refuses device files including pipes (SpecialFileError), absolute link targets (AbsoluteLinkError), links resolving outside destination (LinkOutsideDestinationError), and since 3.14 raises LinkFallbackError when link emulation would itself be rejected.

libarchive security flags SECURE_SYMLINKS, SECURE_NODOTDOT, SECURE_NOABSOLUTEPATHS are opt-in and off by default; absolute paths are permitted by default; SECURE_SYMLINKS with UNLINK removes intermediate symlinks; a trailing .. always errors.
Sockets carry no persistent content and should be recorded type-only or refused.
decision_needed: Are sockets an Entrybound EntryKind (type-only) or refused at capture?

statement: Device nodes (block/char) should require an explicit privileged restoration mode; FIFOs likewise refused by safe default (as Python data filter does).
decision_needed: What explicit mode enables device/FIFO restoration in Entrybound?

statement: Hardlinks need a documented resolution model: first occurrence wins, the link target must be a member already emitted, and a hardlink to a symlink must be disambiguated.
research_needed: Check Entrybound EAM hardlink model and ordering invariant; add conformance vectors for forward-reference and hardlink-to-symlink.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound model hardlinks (grouping vs target reference), and what ordering constraint applies?

statement: Linux filenames are arbitrary byte strings excluding NUL and '/'; the kernel declares no encoding; pax provides charset and hdrcharset so archives declare rather than guess.
research_needed: Measure prevalence of non-UTF-8 names in real Linux trees to size the impact of UTF-8-only LogicalPath.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound admit non-UTF-8 path components (currently excluded per README) and how are they declared?

statement: APFS is normalization-preserving and normalization-insensitive (hashes normalized form); HFS+ stores the normalized (NFD) form on disk; APFS uses Unicode 9.0, HFS+ Unicode 3.2; both case-insensitive by default on macOS with case-sensitive variants; iOS is case-sensitive only.
Archives created from HFS+ carry NFD-mangled names, and round-tripping names HFS+ to APFS is not identity.
Windows filenames are UTF-16 code units (unpaired surrogates storable), with reserved names, trailing dot/space stripping, and case-insensitivity by default.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound capture Windows names containing unpaired surrogates (refuse, escape, or loss record)?

statement: Collision classes to detect: case-fold (README/readme), NFC/NFD (cafe two ways), Windows reserved-name (nul.txt), trailing dot/space (a. vs a), and Unicode confusables.
research_needed: Check Entrybound collision-detection coverage per class; confusable detection needs a defined Unicode data version (UTS #39).
decision_needed: Which collision classes does Entrybound detect (confusables included?) and with which Unicode version?

statement: Architecture: the archive stores the exact name byte sequence plus a declared encoding; the writer must not normalize.
research_needed: Compare with Entrybound LogicalPath rules (UTF-8 requirement, normalization policy).
decision_needed: Does Entrybound LogicalPath preserve exact bytes without normalization, and is encoding declared?

statement: The extractor is required by spec to detect and refuse name collisions on the target platform, rather than the writer normalizing.
Tension: the section says collision classes must be detected 'at write time' yet assigns detection and refusal to the extractor; whether writers also diagnose portable-name hazards is unresolved.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound pack emit diagnostics for cross-platform collision hazards in addition to extractor refusal?

statement: openat2(2) (Linux 5.6) provides RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (all components, implies NO_MAGICLINKS), RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, RESOLVE_NO_XDEV (no mount traversal incl. bind mounts), and RESOLVE_CACHED (5.12, optimization not security).
RESOLVE_IN_ROOT and RESOLVE_BENEATH can return EAGAIN when the kernel cannot guarantee .. did not escape under concurrent rename/mount; callers must retry with a bounded attempt count.
RESOLVE_NO_XDEV should be configurable rather than unconditional, since indiscriminate use may cause spurious errors where bind mounts appear.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound expose a mount-crossing policy option for extraction, and what is the default?

statement: Recommendation: use RESOLVE_IN_ROOT for the extractor so absolute symlinks in the archive resolve inside the destination rather than failing.
research_needed: Check whether cap-std on Linux uses openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH/IN_ROOT; compare semantics with Entrybound symlink policy.
decision_needed: Should extraction interpret archive absolute symlinks relative to the destination root (IN_ROOT) or refuse them (BENEATH / Python data filter)?

statement: Tension: recommending RESOLVE_IN_ROOT makes absolute symlinks resolve inside destination, whereas the cited Python data filter refuses absolute link targets outright; the preferred policy for absolute symlink members is unresolved.
decision_needed: What is Entrybound's policy for symlink members with absolute targets: refuse, rewrite, or resolve-in-root?

statement: open_tree(2)/move_mount(2) arrived in Linux 5.2 (glibc 2.36), open_tree_attr in 6.15; OPEN_TREE_CLONE (needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN) with AT_RECURSIVE creates a detached bind mount destroyed when its fd closes unless attached, giving a private disposable destination mount.
Mount namespaces (unshare CLONE_NEWNS plus pivot_root) remain the strongest containment but require privilege.

Landlock introduced in Linux 5.13 (needs CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK and LSM enablement); ABI 1 5.13 fs rights, 2 5.19 REFER, 3 6.2 TRUNCATE, 4 6.7 TCP, 5 6.10 IOCTL_DEV, 6 6.12 IPC scoping, 7 6.15 audit flags, 8 7.0 RESTRICT_SELF_TSYNC.
Landlock ABI 9 (FS_RESOLVE_UNIX) and ABI 10 (UDP, quiet rule flags) are documented but their kernel versions are unverified (plausibly 7.1/7.2).
research_needed: Confirm from kernel release notes.

statement: Landlock supports at most 16 stacked rulesets and cannot restrict chdir, stat, flock, chmod, chown, setxattr, utime, fcntl or access; files opened before sandboxing stay unrestricted; overlayfs layers do not inherit restrictions (bind mounts do).
Landlock alone does not secure a metadata-restoring extractor, because the metadata pass (chmod/chown/utimensat/setxattr) is outside its control.
research_needed: Security review of Entrybound metadata restore path for by-path operations.

statement: seccomp filters syscalls without path visibility; it complements (e.g. forbidding mknod, mount, chroot) but is never a path-confinement mechanism.
On macOS AT_RESOLVE_BENEATH does not exist; open(2) documents O_NOFOLLOW_ANY (fail if any path component is a symlink) and O_RESOLVE_BENEATH (openat fails if resolution escapes the dirfd directory).

openat() present since OS X 10.10; the open(2) man page does not state when O_NOFOLLOW_ANY was introduced (cap-std issue attributes it to macOS 11, secondary source); introduction version of O_RESOLVE_BENEATH also not stated.
research_needed: Determine minimum macOS versions for O_NOFOLLOW_ANY and O_RESOLVE_BENEATH.
decision_needed: What minimum macOS version does Entrybound require for kernel-enforced confinement, and what is the fallback?

statement: sandbox_init(3) is deprecated; built-in profiles must not be used when building against macOS SDK 27.0 or later and processes opting in are killed; entitlement-based App Sandbox is the only supported route.
refines_or_supersedes: Corrects premise that sandbox_init is merely deprecated
research_needed: Exclude sandbox_init from Entrybound macOS confinement design.

statement: Win32 has no openat2 equivalent; CreateFile with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT opens a reparse point itself, the primitive for inspecting rather than traversing junctions/symlinks.

NtCreateFile is the only true relative open on Windows (OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES.RootDirectory handle plus relative ObjectName); with FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT it opens the reparse point without normal reparse processing; OBJ_CASE_INSENSITIVE is documented.
research_needed: Assess availability through safe Rust (cap-std/winapi-util) versus unsafe FFI to ntdll.

statement: OBJ_DONT_REPARSE is not documented on the NtCreateFile page; its availability and semantics are unverified.
research_needed: Find primary documentation for OBJ_DONT_REPARSE and minimum Windows version.

statement: The \\?\ prefix takes trailing dots/spaces, reserved device names and ./.. literally; necessary for fidelity but shifts the entire validation burden to the extractor.

Avoid junction escape on Windows by walking the destination one component at a time with relative NtCreateFile from the parent handle plus FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, checking the reparse tag before descending; never pass a multi-component path to the kernel.
research_needed: Verify cap-std Windows implementation performs per-component reparse checks; fuzz with junction swaps.

statement: Hold the root directory handle for the whole extraction, on Windows opened without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so the root cannot be renamed or deleted underneath (as Go os.Root does).
research_needed: Check whether cap-std Dir on Windows opens without FILE_SHARE_DELETE.

statement: Go os.Root was added in Go 1.24 with Create, Lstat, Mkdir, Open, OpenFile, OpenRoot, Remove, Stat; Unix uses openat family with a pinned root fd; Windows holds a handle preventing rename/deletion and blocks reserved device names; WASI uses preview-1 sandboxing; GOOS=js is TOCTOU-vulnerable; Plan 9 lexical sanitization.
Go os.Root documented gaps: does not prevent mount-point traversal on Unix; TOCTOU on Node; initially lacked symlink creation and rename; performance cost proportional to path depth.
research_needed: Measure per-depth cost of component-wise resolution in Entrybound extraction at path depth up to 1,024.

statement: Go 1.26 release notes mention nothing about os.Root, archive/tar, sparse or traversal security; whether Go 1.25 expanded os.Root (issue 67002: Symlink/Rename) is unverified.
research_needed: Read Go 1.25 release notes and issue 67002 status.

statement: cap-std 4.0.3 docs describe a capability-based std-like API (Dir for open directories, Pool for network addresses) but the front page does not document per-platform implementation, TOCTOU behaviour, or platform gaps.
'cap-std uses openat2' on Linux is unverified from primary docs.
research_needed: Read cap-primitives source for Linux resolution path (openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH vs manual component walk) at 4.0.3; relevant because Entrybound confinement depends on cap-std.

statement: cap-std issue #179 (open since 2021-08-20) states cap-std uses a slower manual component-by-component validation on macOS instead of O_NOFOLLOW_ANY, and it also does not use O_RESOLVE_BENEATH; this manual pattern carries residual TOCTOU exposure.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (GitHub issue #179) plus inference on TOCTOU
research_needed: Audit cap-std 4.0.3 macOS path resolution; race-test concurrent symlink swaps during Entrybound extraction on macOS; security review.
decision_needed: Is cap-std's macOS confinement acceptable for Entrybound v1 or must a kernel-enforced O_RESOLVE_BENEATH path be added?

statement: libarchive archive_write_disk: all security flags are opt-in (absolute paths permitted by default); ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_ACL, _XATTR, _FFLAGS, _MAC_METADATA are ignored by default.
ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SPARSE scans data for NUL blocks and recreates holes regardless of what the archive recorded, i.e. libarchive invents sparseness.
research_needed: Decide whether Entrybound extractor may create holes for zero runs independent of recorded map.
decision_needed: May Entrybound extraction punch holes for zero runs not recorded as sparse (policy option)?

statement: On EAGAIN from RESOLVE_BENEATH/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, use a bounded retry loop then hard fail; never fall back to string validation.
decision_needed: What retry bound does Entrybound use for EAGAIN resolution failures, and is the failure a distinct diagnostic reason code?

statement: Guard against mount-point substitution under the destination via RESOLVE_NO_XDEV where the environment is controlled, otherwise a private mount namespace or open_tree(OPEN_TREE_CLONE|AT_RECURSIVE) detached mount.
research_needed: Threat-model whether unprivileged extraction can defend against mount substitution at all.

statement: The metadata pass is unprotected: Landlock cannot restrict chmod/chown/setxattr/utime and there is no chmodat2/chownat2 accepting RESOLVE_* flags.

Never touch metadata by path: open the object once with openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS) then apply fchmod, fchown, futimens, fsetxattr on that fd, or /proc/self/fd/N where no f-variant exists; for symlinks use O_PATH plus /proc/self/fd.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound restore code for by-path metadata calls; check safe-Rust availability of fd-based xattr/utimens (rustix, cap-std fs_utf8/ext).
decision_needed: Does Entrybound apply all restored metadata through handles/fds rather than paths on every platform?

statement: Always create final components with O_CREAT|O_EXCL; on collision unlink via the parent fd and retry; never O_TRUNC onto an existing path.
decision_needed: What overwrite policy options exist beyond Refuse, and do they unlink-via-parent-handle rather than truncate?

statement: Hold the root fd/handle for the whole extraction so the root cannot disappear underneath.
Maintain an explicit stack of directory fds and resolve exactly one component per syscall; any path that reconstructs and re-opens a full path reintroduces the race.
research_needed: Code audit of Entrybound extractor for full-path re-open patterns (including cap-std internals).

statement: Hardlink-to-symlink handling and link-emulation fallbacks (extracting a second copy) must re-apply all filters, since emulation can smuggle a member past them (Python LinkFallbackError, 3.14).
decision_needed: When hardlink creation fails, does Entrybound copy-emulate, and if so is the emulated copy re-validated?

statement: PEP 706 (Final, Python 3.12) added filter= to TarFile.extract/extractall with fully_trusted, tar and data levels; CPython 3.14.7 docs confirm the endpoint.
Python tar filter strips leading / and os.sep, refuses absolute paths, normalizes .. via normpath, refuses members outside destination, and clears setuid/setgid/sticky and group/other write.

Python data filter adds: normalized link targets, refuses absolute or outside links, refuses devices and pipes, sets owner rw and strips group/other execute on regular files, skips permissions for other types, and ignores ownership entirely (uid/gid/uname/gname None).
research_needed: Compare Entrybound default extraction policy against data filter line by line (incumbent capability matrix).
decision_needed: Does Entrybound default extraction ignore ownership like Python's data filter?

statement: Python 3.14 default extraction filter is 'data' (previously fully_trusted); resolution order is explicit filter=, then TarFile.extraction_filter, then 'data'; errorlevel >=1 aborts, 0 skips and logs; PEP 721 mandates tarfile.data_filter for sdist extraction.

CPython warns tarfile is unsuitable for untrusted files even with data filter without extra checks (disk quotas, memory limits, filename validation); the data filter is a metadata sanitizer, not a confinement mechanism, and does not use openat2.
Design goal: the Entrybound extractor should close the gap by combining metadata sanitization with kernel-level confinement and resource limits (quotas, memory, filename validation).
research_needed: Adversarial test corpus comparing Entrybound vs Python data filter, libarchive, Go os.Root on traversal, link, device, and budget attacks.

statement: Superiority claim implied: a confinement-based extractor is safer than string-validating sanitizers such as Python's data filter.
research_needed: Demonstrate with race/exploit test cases that sanitizer-only extractors fail where Entrybound succeeds.

statement: RFC 6838 media type trees: standards tree (IETF/SDOs, RFC required, no faceted names), vnd. (anyone for public products, Expert Review, RFC optional), prs. (experimental/non-commercial, Expert Review), x. (cannot be registered, private use, strongly discouraged).

Registration procedure: preliminary review on media-types@iana.org (required for standards tree, encouraged otherwise), submit via iana.org/form/media-types, Expert Review by the Applications Area-appointed reviewer, then IANA publishes.

IANA media type template requires: type/subtype, required/optional parameters, encoding, security and interoperability considerations, published specification, applications, fragment identifiers, magic numbers, file extensions, Mac type codes, contact, intended usage, restrictions, author, change controller.
research_needed: Draft Entrybound registration template; requires frozen magic, extension, published spec URL, security considerations.
decision_needed: Who is the change controller and contact for the Entrybound media type registration?

statement: IANA registration turnaround is unverified; author infers vendor-tree registrations with clean template and public spec clear Expert Review in weeks, standards-tree takes months to years.
research_needed: Examine recent vnd. registration histories (request to publication dates).

statement: Recent archive-type registrations include application/gzip, epub+zip, lpf+zip, p21+zip, aas+zip, automationml-amlx+zip, bacnet-xdd+zip, vnd.etsi.asic-s/e+zip, vnd.comicbook+zip, vnd.eln+zip, vnd.dece.zip, vec-package+zip/+gzip and many vnd.*+zip entries.
The IANA application registry fetch truncated alphabetically around 'g', so application/zip, x-tar, zstd and all later archive types are absent from the survey.
research_needed: Fetch the full IANA application registry and complete the archive-type survey.

statement: Modern container formats register in the vendor tree with a +zip structured syntax suffix; the standards tree is effectively closed to non-SDO work; a new structured suffix requires a standards-track document.

Because Entrybound's native container is not ZIP-based, the recommended registration is application/vnd.<org>.<name> without a +zip suffix; seeking a new structured suffix only if a generalizable container is defined.
decision_needed: What media type name (vnd. vs prs., org segment) will Entrybound register, and will it pursue a structured suffix?

statement: PNG 1.2 rationale for signature 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A: 0x89 non-ASCII catches text misrecognition and bit-7 stripping; 'PNG' names the format; CR-LF catches newline alteration; 0x1A stops MS-DOS display; final LF catches inverse CR-LF translation; first two bytes distinguish on two-byte-type systems.
PNG Third Edition (W3C Rec 2025-06-24) keeps the same 8 signature bytes but dropped the per-byte rationale; cite the PNG 1.2 rationale document for reasoning.
Magic number criteria: at least 8 bytes at offset 0, containing a byte >= 0x80, a CR-LF pair and a bare LF, a 0x1A or 0x00, a human-readable ASCII tag, and a version/generation byte.
research_needed: Evaluate Entrybound's chosen magic against each criterion; test newline-translation and 7-bit transport detection.
decision_needed: Does the Entrybound magic satisfy the PNG-derived criteria, and is it frozen?

statement: The magic must not be a prefix of any registered magic in libmagic's database.
research_needed: Run the Entrybound magic against the current file/libmagic Magdir for prefix collisions.

statement: Add a trailer magic plus a total-length field so truncation is distinguishable from corruption.
research_needed: Check Entrybound footer design for trailer magic and total length; add truncation conformance vectors.
decision_needed: Does the Entrybound footer carry a trailer magic and total archive length enabling truncation-vs-corruption diagnosis?

statement: Archives are the one format class where truncation is the dominant real-world failure mode.
research_needed: Gather empirical data on archive failure modes (truncated downloads vs bit rot vs media errors).

statement: libmagic magic lines have offset (may be negative from EOF or indirect), type, test, message; > prefixes build hierarchical tests; directives !:mime, !:ext, !:apple and !:strength (operator +-*/ with 0-255) adjust match ranking.
research_needed: Author libmagic entry with !:mime and !:ext once media type and extension are frozen; consider negative-offset trailer test.

statement: libmagic full strength tie-breaking algorithm and upstream file project contribution process are unverified.
research_needed: Read file(1) source for strength algorithm and project contribution guidance.

statement: freedesktop shared-mime-info spec is version 0.21 dated 2018-10-02; formats ship XML with mime-type, glob patterns and prioritized magic match elements installed to /usr/share/mime/packages/ and compiled by update-mime-database; it stores no user preferences.
shared-mime-info upstream contribution process is unverified (gitlab.freedesktop.org robots-disallowed and proxy-blocked).
research_needed: Read shared-mime-info CONTRIBUTING.md.

statement: Practical route: register the IANA media type first, then submit libmagic and shared-mime-info entries citing it, because both projects treat an existing registration as the strongest evidence a type is real.
research_needed: Confirm upstream acceptance criteria for new format entries.
decision_needed: What is the Entrybound identification registration sequence and timing relative to v1 release?

statement: Library of Congress Sustainability of Digital Formats (updated 2025-02-14) lists seven factors: disclosure, adoption, transparency, self-documentation, external dependencies, impact of patents, technical protection mechanisms, plus content-specific quality/functionality factors.
Transparency factor argues against compressing the metadata index: preservationists want to read the manifest with head and strings; recommend an uncompressed, human-inspectable manifest.
research_needed: Measure manifest size cost of uncompressed vs compressed encoding at 1M entries; check tension with encrypted-metadata privacy features.
decision_needed: Is the Entrybound manifest stored uncompressed/inspectable by default, and how does that interact with encrypted metadata?

statement: Tension: transparency (uncompressed human-inspectable manifest) and 'do not make encryption structural' may conflict with Entrybound features such as compressed manifests or encrypted metadata/privacy.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound reconcile preservation transparency with metadata compression and confidentiality?

statement: Self-documentation factor: the format should carry its own version, its declared capability set, and ideally a human-readable prologue.
decision_needed: Will Entrybound include a human-readable prologue in the preamble, and are feature bits self-describing?

statement: PRONOM (UK National Archives) is the technical format registry whose signatures drive DROID, the identification tool preservation repositories run; it assigns PUIDs; PRONOM registration is separate from IANA.
The PRONOM submission form fields are unverified (submitinfo page robots-disallowed).
research_needed: Retrieve the PRONOM submission form requirements.

statement: DPC Digital Preservation Handbook criteria: open vs proprietary (export capability matters), well-documented and widely implemented standards, listing in PRONOM, adoption level, lossless encoding for masters, metadata support, significant properties; recommends validation tools such as JHOVE and reducing format proliferation.
research_needed: Assess whether Entrybound adds to format proliferation concerns and whether a JHOVE-style validator module is needed.

statement: Preservation guidance: archival masters should use lossless encoding, with lossy encoding reserved for access copies; any lossy transform must be clearly distinguishable from archival content.
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound reconstructive transforms (DEFLATE/JPEG) are bit-exact and any lossy option is labelled distinctly in identity and reports.
decision_needed: Is any lossy recompression permitted in Entrybound archives, and how is it marked relative to archival identity?

statement: Preservation guidance: identify and document significant properties and provide format validation tooling (JHOVE-style) for the format.
decision_needed: Will Entrybound publish a significant-properties statement and a JHOVE module or equivalent validator?

statement: Open Preservation Foundation guidance was not fetched.
research_needed: Review OPF published guidance on new format adoption and validators.

statement: Historical format success/failure case studies were not researched; the author declines to supply unsourced citations.
research_needed: Research historical archive/format longevity case studies (e.g. ARC, StuffIt, ZIP extensions).

statement: PNG Third Edition (2025) keeps the 1996 signature bit-identical about 29 years later, an existence proof for a thirty-year target.

PNG's longevity ingredients are a standards-body-maintained normative spec, a magic designed for hostile transports, a chunked container with unknown chunks skippable by construction, and multiple independent implementations.
evidence_in_source: analysis grounded in verified PNG facts
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound container unknown-section skippability semantics mirror PNG ancillary chunk rules.
decision_needed: Are unknown Entrybound sections skippable by construction with a critical/ancillary distinction?

statement: pax was republished unchanged in substance in IEEE 1003.1-2024 so 1990s pax archives still read, while GNU sparse 0.0 and 0.1 are effectively unreadable by non-GNU tools (0.0 violates POSIX keyword semantics, 0.1 relies on a GNU-specific name convention).
Lesson: within one format family, normatively specified parts survived and implementation-specified parts did not.
research_needed: Broader case-study evidence across format families.

statement: A normative spec plus reference test vectors is necessary but not sufficient for thirty-year readability.
Thirty-year deliverable: a normative specification at a stable, archived, versioned URL with a change controller identified in the IANA registration.
decision_needed: Where will the Entrybound normative spec be published and archived with stable versioned URLs?

statement: Thirty-year deliverable: reference test vectors including deliberately malformed ones, plus a validator, so future implementers can prove conformance without the original code (LoC disclosure includes validation tools).
evidence_in_source: synthesis grounded in LoC disclosure wording
research_needed: Inventory Entrybound conformance corpus coverage of malformed inputs.
decision_needed: Is a standalone validator (verify command or separate tool) part of the v1 disclosure deliverable?

statement: Thirty-year deliverable: byte-level transparency via an uncompressed human-inspectable manifest and a magic number, so the format degrades to strings/head rather than nothing.
Thirty-year deliverable: registered identity in three places: IANA media type, libmagic/shared-mime-info entry, and PRONOM PUID; without PRONOM preservation tooling cannot name the file.
decision_needed: Which identification registrations are committed for Entrybound and when?

statement: Thirty-year deliverable: a second independent implementation, the only real test that the spec says what is intended.
research_needed: Build or commission an independent minimal reader from the spec alone and diff outcomes on the corpus.
decision_needed: Will an independent (possibly minimal, non-Rust) reader be produced before or after v1 freeze?

statement: Thirty-year deliverable: no external hardware/OS/software dependencies, no patents, no technical protection mechanisms (LoC factors 5-7).
research_needed: Patent review of codecs and crypto primitives used by Entrybound.

statement: Do not mandate a compression codec the format owner does not control.
research_needed: Evaluate Entrybound mandatory codec set (e.g. zstd/LZMA2) for spec stability, independent implementations, and control.
decision_needed: Which codecs are mandatory for an Entrybound v1 reader, and is each independently specified and implementable?

statement: Do not make encryption structural to the archive format (encryption should not be required to read unencrypted archives or block preservation).
decision_needed: Is Entrybound encryption an optional layer such that non-encrypted archives never require crypto code to read?

statement: Explicit declaration of what was not preserved: every platform loses something (btime, idmapped uid, decmpfs), so loss should be a first-class, typed, in-band record making archive fidelity assessable decades later.
evidence_in_source: synthesis from Part A (not in any external checklist)
research_needed: Check whether Entrybound FidelityReport/loss records are stored in-band in the archive at capture, not only emitted at extraction.
decision_needed: Are capture-time metadata losses recorded in-band in the Entrybound archive as typed records?

statement: Windows FILE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPRESSED / FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ENCRYPTED and EFS behaviour were not researched.
research_needed: Research capture/restore semantics of NTFS compression and EFS-encrypted files (raw EFS backup APIs).
decision_needed: How does Entrybound capture EFS-encrypted or NTFS-compressed files and report the loss?

statement: Unverified list consolidated: PyPI sparse ban, APFS timestamps, Landlock ABI 9/10 versions, mkfs.xfs bigtime default, idmapped mount kernel version, macOS xattr limits, MOTW propagation by archive formats, IANA turnaround, libmagic/shared-mime-info contribution processes, Go 1.25 os.Root expansion.
research_needed: Assign each item to follow-up research before relying on it in the spec.
